Adding the ops-run excerpt from the runbook for clarity — please follow this verbatim during the activation window: 

--- runbook excerpt (activation window) ---
T-minus 00:10: confirm bridge + recording + stakeholders present.
T-zero (activation start): 
  - Step A: Seed control-plane handshake (API keys rotated into session) — confirm control-plane ACKs within 45s.
  - Step B: KV priming: push 3 synthetic prefixes + 5 warm-up requests to KV store on each serving node (expected time: 8-12 minutes).
  - Step C: Prefix warmup: announce prefixes from ACME side, validate reachability from 3 external vantage points (use vantage-1/2/3).
  - Step D: Traffic ramp: begin 5 qps synthetic ramp (increase 1 qps per 2 minutes) for 15 minutes while monitoring p95/p99.
  - Step E: Smoke probes: run health-check suite (http 200, model checksum, kv latency < 50ms) across 10 endpoints.

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback to prior routing if any of below):
  - Control-plane handshake fails more than twice consecutively within 10m.
  - KV priming reports >20% missing keys across nodes after 12m.
  - Application error rate >15% sustained for more than 5 minutes.
  - Packet loss >1% or p99 latency >350ms compared to baseline.

If a controlled rollback is triggered: revert announcements and re-establish prior BGP sessions; expected customer-visible disruption is <10 minutes for a controlled rollback (most services will reconnect transparently). Full revert to prior routing (more conservative) can be expected to take 25–40 minutes depending on downstream caches and DNS TTLs — plan accordingly.

I'll be on the bridge to coordinate the KV priming and prefix validation.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
